advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the LockTimeout docstring example to show `pid_state=live` (matching the actual rendered key at lock.py:363).
evidence: src/rebar/_store/lock.py:110: `(holder: host=name-h pid=4321 start=93117 held=48s pid=live)`
Test asserts the real key: tests/unit/test_lock_timeout_names_holder_7084.py `assert "pid_state=live" in holder`
advisory.finding: The LockTimeout docstring example renders the liveness field as 'pid=live', but the code emits the key 'pid_state=live'. The example does not match actual output, and would mislead operators/readers matching on the example format.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the docstring example line 110 from `... held=48s pid=live)` to `... held=48s pid_state=live)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have _describe_stamped_pid qualify 'live' with the stamped vs current process start time (as _mkdir_lock_is_stale does) so a recycled pid is not reported as a live holder.
evidence: Reclamation path additionally checks start time: src/rebar/_store/lock.py:505-509 `stamped_start = ... current_start = _process_start_time(pid) ... if stamped_start is not None and current_start is not None and stamped_start != current_start: return True` (recycled pid => stale)
describe_lock_holder docstring asserts the parallel: src/rebar/_store/lock.py:328-330 'a dead one => a stale stamp the reclamation path will clear'
advisory.finding: _describe_stamped_pid reports 'live' from _pid_alive alone and omits the recycled-pid start-time qualification that _mkdir_lock_is_stale applies, so a recycled pid (a different process wearing the same number) is reported 'pid_state=live' even though reclamation would classify that stamp as stale — contradicting the function's own claim to mirror the reclamation liveness verdict.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that seeds a local-host stamp with a mismatched ns and asserts 'unprobeable (other pid namespace)'.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/lock.py:382-384: `stamped_ns = None if fields["ns"] == _STAMP_UNKNOWN else fields["ns"]` then `if stamped_ns != _read_pid_namespace_id(): return "unprobeable (other pid namespace)"`

Tests cover foreign-host, live, and not-running verdicts (test_a_foreign_host_stamp_is_reported_unprobeable, test_a_dead_stamped_pid_reports_not_running, test_describes_a_held_lock_from_the_existing_stamp) but no test asserts 'unprobeable (other pid namespace)'.
src/rebar/_store/lock.py:385-388: `try: pid = int(fields["pid"]) except ValueError: return "unprobeable (malformed pid)"`
No test in tests/unit/test_lock_timeout_names_holder_7084.py seeds a non-integer pid with matching host/ns.
advisory.finding: The 'unprobeable (other pid namespace)' verdict branch of _describe_stamped_pid is never exercised: no test seeds a stamp with the local host identity but a differing ns field. A regression that dropped or inverted the namespace check would go undetected.
merged_from: The 'unprobeable (malformed pid)' branch of _describe_stamped_pid is untested: no test seeds a v2 stamp whose pid field is non-integer while host and ns match locally, so the ValueError→'unprobeable (malformed pid)' path never runs.
scenarios: A stamp written by a process in a different PID namespace on the same host.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that makes the fcntl leg succeed but the mkdir leg time out and assert the raised LockTimeout still names the holder.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/lock.py:655-659: `if dual_window: if not _acquire_mkdir(lock_dir, deadline): holder = describe_lock_holder(tracker)  # read before releasing our fcntl leg / os.close(fd) / raise LockTimeout(total_wait, holder)`
test_contended_timeout_names_the_holder drives a full acquire that times out on the fcntl leg (another process holds it); no test forces the mkdir leg to fail while fcntl succeeds.
advisory.finding: The mkdir-leg timeout path — where the holder is read into a local before os.close(fd) and then LockTimeout(total_wait, holder) is raised — is not exercised by any test. The contended end-to-end test only drives the fcntl leg (fd == -1), leaving the second raise site and the read-before-release ordering unverified.
scenarios: fcntl acquired locally but the mkdir ownership leg times out (dual_window contention).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert start=<value> is present for a known start and absent when the stamp's start is the unknown sentinel.
evidence: test_describes_a_held_lock_from_the_existing_stamp asserts host/pid/held/pid_state but never asserts on start=; test_a_foreign_host_stamp_is_reported_unprobeable seeds start=99 but does not assert start= appears.
advisory.finding: The conditional rendering of the start= field is never asserted: no test checks that a present start value appears as start=<value>, nor that a _STAMP_UNKNOWN start is omitted from the phrase.
scenarios: Stamp with a known start time; stamp with start=- (unknown).
